analysis.completion_evidence: Final diff shows fly.yml actions pinned (checkout@v7, setup-flyctl@1.6), Dockerfile BUN_VERSION=1.4.0, bun.lock deleted, and the assistant reports 588 insertions / 2,187 deletions across 27 files plus 6 new. Outcome signals show npm install resolving vitest/coverage-v8 to 4.1.10, tsc --noEmit exit 0 (also with --strict), `vp test run` passing, `vp build` succeeding, and sitemap.xml/rss.xml served with correct content under bun. Final assistant text reports commit pushed (remote main at 8b8d00a), CI green, deployed, /blog payload 46,082→32,174 bytes. The Bun markdown swap (#11,#12,#14) was explicitly skipped with stated blockers; the user did not object.
analysis.notes: Outcome signals say 'Files touched: none' but the linked-commit diff and assistant text show extensive edits, tests and builds; classified as edit+tests. The final assistant text says 'I pushed normally rather than with --force' as a 'deviation from what you asked', implying the user requested a (force) push, but the visible turn 5 only says 'i dont need redesign' — the commit/push instruction is inferred and may have been truncated from the transcript. 'fix everything' was not literally fully met (Bun parser swap #11/#12/#14 skipped) but was explicitly justified and the user did not object, so c10 covers it and completion is marked yes. Test runs exercise c4 (vitest pin), c6 (summary DTO tests) and c9 (sanitizer tests); other criteria are diff/judge-based.
analysis.task_statement: The user asked for a code review of their TanStack Start blog (xiaofeng-blog) focused on dependency upgrades and replacing old libraries, then asked the assistant to re-evaluate in light of Bun 1.4's native markdown support and current web trends, produce a consolidated table of recommended changes, and finally implement all of them. The session ended with the changes committed, pushed, CI green and deployed, with the Bun-native markdown swap explicitly skipped as blocked and the AI palette left unverified at the user's request.
